correctness.rationale: For every alpha>0 the integration-by-parts identity (alpha+n)I_n+(alpha-n+2)I_(n-2)=2cos((n-1)pi/2) follows with legitimate endpoints. Even coefficients are all positive when 0<alpha<2 and the fourth is negative when alpha>2. The exact fifth coefficient is alpha(alpha^2-16alpha+23)/(5(alpha+1)(alpha+3)(alpha+5)), so the unique threshold in (0,2) is 8-sqrt(41). Odd n>=7 are strictly positive by the proved two-step recurrence lower bound, including the equality case at n=5. The nonnegative Fourier characterization implies global positive semidefiniteness and consecutive positive frequencies yield strictness by Vandermonde. CHECK.py ran from its packaged source path and passed exact sympy identities, 384 direct quadrature comparisons (worst error 4.744e-14), and a 32-site negative eigenvalue witness at alpha=1.7. These experiments are not used as infinite-frequency proof.

value.rationale: Gneiting (2011) expressly motivates the generalized sine-power family and asks for its positivity parameter region; support radius c=pi/2 is geometrically natural as half the maximal circle distance. The exact radical smoothness threshold and its uniquely vanishing fifth harmonic resolve a sharp, nontrivial section of that problem, reaching exponents above one beyond elementary convexity-based sufficient criteria. The endpoint remains strictly positive definite, yielding a useful distinction between spectral nonnegativity and strict finite-set positivity. This is a complete natural one-parameter classification, not an arbitrary tiny numerical extension.
